about: Pass 10 (2026-10-10): independent multi-model LLM evaluations in openly licensed (CC BY / CC BY-SA / CC0) arXiv papers from 2026-04..2026-10. Numbers transcribed from the HTML table text of the pinned version; percentages divided by 100.

benchmarks.name: PureDocBench document parsing (Avg3 over Clean/Digital/Real)
benchmarks.description: PureDocBench (arXiv:2605.07492v2, CC BY 4.0): full-page document parsing of 1,475 generated source pages in 10 domains, each as matched Clean, Digital-degraded and Real (recaptured) images (4,425 images). OmniDocBench framework: per-track Overall = ((1-TextEdit)x100 + FormulaCDM + TableTEDS)/3; score = mean of the three track Overalls (Avg3), Table 2 'Overall', stored /100.

benchmarks.name: SWE Atlas (Codebase Q&A, Test Writing, Refactoring; mini-SWE-agent) pass@1
benchmarks.description: SWE Atlas (arXiv:2605.08366v1, CC BY 4.0): 284 expert-authored software-engineering tasks from 18 open-source repositories - Codebase Q&A (124), Test Writing (90) and Refactoring (70) - verified by programmatic checks (tests, mutation testing) plus rubric-based LLM-judge grading. Score = Pass@1 averaged over 3 trials with the minimal mini-SWE-agent (bash-only) scaffold in Harbor, highest thinking setting per Table 8 (Table 1).

benchmarks.name: DiagnosticIQ industrial maintenance MCQ (macro accuracy, 4 options)
benchmarks.description: DiagnosticIQ (arXiv:2605.08614v1, CC BY 4.0): 6,690 four-option multiple-choice questions generated from 118 expert-curated industrial monitoring rules (HVAC/AHU, pumps, chillers ...): given an asset description and the rule's triggered sensor conditions, select (or eliminate) the correct maintenance observation/action. Zero-shot direct prompting, temperature 0, max 4,096 tokens; missing answers count as wrong. Score = accuracy macro-averaged over asset classes (Table 2 'Macro % D.IQ'); chance 25%.

benchmarks.name: ContractBench success rate (33 observation-contract tool tasks)
benchmarks.description: ContractBench (arXiv:2605.17281v2, CC BY 4.0): 33 programmatically validated tool-use agent tasks that test whether an agent preserves 'observation contracts' (temporal validity of presigned URLs/tokens under a virtual clock, and byte-level integrity checked by SHA-256). Success rate = passed episodes / 99 (33 tasks x k=3 rollouts, temperature 0, 600 s per episode), as printed in Table 10 (SR%).

benchmarks.name: ChartArena chart parsing (English, mAP_high average)
benchmarks.description: ChartArena (arXiv:2606.01348v3, CC BY 4.0): chart-to-structure parsing across eight chart families (bar, line, pie, radar, box plot, combination, flowchart, mind map) and three visual scenarios (digital rendering, printed photo, hand-drawn photo). Outputs in any format are normalised to triples (numeric charts) or labelled graphs (diagrams) and scored by mAP at the 'high' tolerance; score = English 'Average' column of Table 2 / Table C.3, stored /100.

benchmarks.name: K-BrowseComp-Verified (Korean web-browsing agent questions, pass@1)
benchmarks.description: K-BrowseComp (arXiv:2606.02404v1, CC BY 4.0): 300 human-verified BrowseComp-style questions grounded in Korean contexts (multi-hop or parallel-constraint, >=4 steps). Agents run in Perplexity's search_evals deep-research agent with Perplexity Search and a budget of 10 search calls per question; final answers extracted by GPT-5.4-mini and matched to gold. Score = single-run accuracy (pass@1) on the Verified subset (Table 2).

benchmarks.name: KINA (Knowledge Index of Noah's Ark) accuracy, 899 ten-option items
benchmarks.description: KINA (arXiv:2606.05104v2, CC BY 4.0): 899 expert-written pseudo-multiple-choice knowledge items across 12 disciplines / 261 subfields; each item has 10 combinatorial options over several statements (chance 10%). Score = overall avg@4 accuracy, default temperature, 32K max new tokens, reasoning budget 16K or 'Medium', no tools (Table 3 'ALL').

benchmarks.name: SurgiQ surgical MCQ (zero-shot, log-probability scoring)
benchmarks.description: SurgiQ (arXiv:2606.08071v1, CC BY 4.0): ~13k four-option multiple-choice questions generated from surgical textbooks across six specialties (physician-audited, near-duplicate filtered). Zero-shot fixed prompt; the answer is the option letter with the highest next-token log-probability (no generated reasoning, so reasoning models are scored without thinking). Score = micro-accuracy over all items (Table 4 'Avg.'); chance 25%.

benchmarks.name: T1-Bench multi-domain conversational agent pass^3
benchmarks.description: T1-Bench (arXiv:2606.11070v1, CC BY 4.0): persistent multi-session tool-using customer-service conversations across 11 travel/dining/shopping domains and multi-domain combinations, with a Gemma4-26B-A4B-it user simulator. A conversation passes only if tool-call recall = 1, parameter recall = 1 and all tool outputs match exactly; score = Pass^K with K=3 (all three of three temperature-1.0 trials pass), averaged over domains (Table 2).

benchmarks.name: Polish medical board exams, bias-mitigated MCQ protocol (7-exam average)
benchmarks.description: Polish Medical Exams re-evaluation (arXiv:2606.12250v1, CC BY-SA 4.0): five-option (A-E) multiple-choice questions from Polish medical and dental final exams (LEK, LDEK), specialist board exams (PES, PESDL, PESF) and English versions of LEK/LDEK. 'OM' protocol: neutral instruction without a sample answer letter, constrained generation to the option letters, temperature 0. Score = mean accuracy over the seven exams (Table 4 'Avg OM'); chance 20%.

benchmarks.name: VisEditBench strict pass rate (1,395 visualization-code editing tasks)
benchmarks.description: VisEditBench (arXiv:2608.10408v1, CC BY 4.0): 1,395 human-annotated tasks where a VLM receives visualization code (Matplotlib/Vega-Lite), a rendered buggy, human-marked or reference chart and an instruction, and must return revised executable code. Zero-shot, temperature 0.2, max 4,096 output tokens. Rendered output passes only if executable, task accuracy >=4.5/5, readability and visual quality >=4/5 and visual similarity >=90 (GPT-4o rubric judge, validated against human ratings). Score = Overall pass rate (Table 2).

benchmarks.name: Diagram-MMU diagram question answering (DQA accuracy, scientific TikZ diagrams)
benchmarks.description: Diagram-MMU (arXiv:2608.12262v1, CC BY 4.0): diagram question answering over 3.7k curated scientific TikZ diagrams in six domains (graph structures, charts, planar geometry, circuits, 3D shapes, chemistry); descriptive, standard-reasoning and what-if questions, two per diagram. Answers extracted and graded 0/1 by Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct (97.5% agreement with humans). Direct answering, temperature 1.0. Score = DQA accuracy (Table 5).

benchmarks.name: BEAR-Bench (bilingual RU/EN enterprise and academic document images, overall accuracy)
benchmarks.description: BEAR-Bench (arXiv:2608.17895v1, CC BY 4.0): 1,000 human-authored question-answer pairs over text-dense professional and academic document images (business 532, science 468; Russian 618, English 382; figures, diagrams, equations). Zero-shot, image + raw question, temperature 0.6; free-form answers judged correct/incorrect by GPT-4o for semantic equivalence. Score = Overall accuracy (Table 2).

benchmarks.name: Thinkingbox-bench pass@1 (507 stateful business-workflow agent tasks, N=20)
benchmarks.description: Thinkingbox-bench (arXiv:2608.19741v4, CC BY 4.0): 507 tool-using agent tasks in five stateful business domains (retail, auto insurance, booking, neobank support, consulting) with MCP-compatible tools, a GPT-5.4-mini simulated user and executable backend-state checks (plus a response rubric on some tasks). A trial passes only if every executable check passes; score = pass@1 micro-averaged over tasks and N=20 independent trials (Table 15 / Table 4 'Average'). Agent temperature 1.0, reasoning effort medium.

benchmarks.name: SciDocBench scientific-document workflows (overall, 496 instances)
benchmarks.description: SciDocBench (arXiv:2609.05141v2, CC BY 4.0): 124 expert-authored, difficulty-screened scientific-research tasks over full papers, multiple papers and associated code/data (seven capability groups, 19 subtasks), each asked in English and Chinese with two document representations (all page images first, or Markdown interleaved) = 496 instances. Scored by deterministic rules, a rubric LLM judge or execution; failures score 0. Score = Overall mean (Table 2), stored /100.

benchmarks.name: GameLogicBench solve rate (72 Godot game-logic tasks, Claude Code scaffold)
benchmarks.description: GameLogicBench (arXiv:2609.21562v2, CC BY 4.0): 72 coding-agent tasks (21 Atom, 28 Combo, 23 Repo) where the agent implements runtime game logic in a Godot 4.4 project; solutions are judged by deterministic tick-level state assertions over hidden scenarios. Score = average solve rate over all tasks (Table 3 'Average'), one sample per configuration, effort=high, 3,600 s limit, egress sealed, Claude Code 2.1.177 scaffold for every imported row.

benchmarks.name: EEGAgentBench overall (tool-based EEG analysis agents, 6 tasks)
benchmarks.description: EEGAgentBench (arXiv:2609.31632v1, CC BY 4.0): 1,072 instances from six public EEG datasets over six tasks - EEG knowledge QA (T1, direct answer) and five tool-based analyses (artifact detection, abnormality screening, dementia cohort classification, seizure event detection, full-night sleep staging) where the agent calls 10 deterministic signal-processing tools before answering. Single run per instance. Score = Overall, the unweighted mean of T1 accuracy, Macro-F1 (T2-T4, T6) and event-based F1 (T5), on a 0-1 scale (Table 2).

benchmarks.name: E2E-SWE (build a working codebase from scratch, 186 tasks) pass@1
benchmarks.description: E2E-SWE (arXiv:2609.38335v1, CC BY 4.0): 186 tasks where an agent must build a complete working repository from a natural-language specification; a task counts only if the generated repository passes every hidden test. Simple ReAct scaffold (bash + edit + submit tools), 4-hour budget, strongest reliable reasoning effort per model; score = pass@1 averaged over 4 independent runs (Table 2).

benchmarks.name: KlinikeBench strict pass@1 (333 interactive clinical encounters, Terminus-2)
benchmarks.description: KlinikeBench (arXiv:2609.38480v2, CC BY 4.0): 333 clinician-authored interactive clinical encounters run in Harbor with the Terminus-2 ReAct harness; the model questions an LLM-simulated patient (GPT-5.4-mini) and executes sandboxed clinical tools. Strict pass@1 = share of tasks with correct diagnosis AND all required tools AND argument-level action constraints AND full must-ask coverage; one rollout per task, medium reasoning effort, 32-turn cap (Table 7).

benchmarks.name: LongSocialBench (full-context, 4-option MCQ over discussion threads)
benchmarks.description: LongSocialBench (arXiv:2610.04118v1, CC BY 4.0): 1,462 human-authored, independently verified four-option questions over complete long online discussion threads (Hacker News, Stack Exchange, Reddit) testing reply-structure-aware social reasoning (six capability surfaces). Full-context prompting: whole serialized thread with reply links + stem + options, one answer letter; exact-match micro accuracy over parsed responses (Table 13 'Full'). Chance 25%.

benchmarks.name: Video2World V2WScore (coding agents reconstruct interactive simulated worlds from videos, OpenCode scaffold)
benchmarks.description: Video2World (arXiv:2610.04432v2, CC BY-SA 4.0): 222 instances (189 embodied manipulation video clips, 39 task families); a coding agent must build an executable physics-simulated scene and robot behaviour that reproduce the video. V2WScore (0-100) combines build rate, task success/progress, geometric fidelity and dynamic fidelity, macro-averaged over task families (Table 2), stored /100. One autonomous attempt per instance, 180-minute limit, OpenCode 1.18.29 scaffold for every imported row (other scaffolds excluded).

benchmarks.name: SpaceCast-Bench predictive spatial reasoning (overall, 16 task types)
benchmarks.description: SpaceCast-Bench (arXiv:2610.12402v1, CC BY 4.0): 3,862 multiple-choice questions from 182 ScanNet/ScanNet++ scenes over 16 task types; the model sees depth-verified view chains and must predict spatial outcomes (direction, distance, occlusion, attributes) after hypothetical camera/object/world transformations at three levels (static, local, global). Chain-of-thought prompt, deterministic decoding. Score = unweighted macro-average of per-task accuracy (Table 1 'Overall'); random baseline 25.9%, humans 87.2%.
